body.statement:
Fix a member of the parameterized late-ramp family and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). For every possibly randomized confidence set \(D_n=D_n(O_n,U)\), where \(U\) is independent of the experiment and has the same law under both signs, if
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\min_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\in D_n\}\ge1-\alpha,
\]
then, for each \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\),
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\Pr_\sigma\!\left\{
 \operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\delta(1-a_\star)\right\}
 \ge a_\star^c-2\alpha.
\]
The bound is nontrivial when \(a_\star^c>2\alpha\). It is an all-confidence-set information bound for the complete logged experiment and does not use a Horvitz--Thompson or AIPW distributional limit.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(m_n=\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor\) and define the late-arm void event
\[
 V_n=\bigcap_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\{A_{nt}=0\}.
\]
By \texttt{def:parameterized-late-ramp-family}, the conditional treatment probability is the deterministic number \(c/t\). Repeated conditioning therefore gives, under either sign,
\[
 \eta_n:=\Pr_\sigma(V_n)
 =\prod_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\left(1-\frac ct\right).
\]
Indeed, if \(V_{n,s}=\bigcap_{t=m_n+1}^{s}\{A_{nt}=0\}\), then \(V_{n,s-1}\in\mathcal F_{n,s-1}\), and \texttt{ass:adaptive-assignment-law} gives
\[
 \Pr_\sigma(V_{n,s})
 =\mathbb E_\sigma\!\left[
  \mathbf 1_{V_{n,s-1}}
  \Pr_\sigma(A_{ns}=0\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1})
 \right]
 =\left(1-\frac cs\right)\Pr_\sigma(V_{n,s-1}).
\]
Iteration proves the product formula. Positivity follows from \(0<c<1\) and \(t\ge1\).

We next evaluate its limit. For \(0\le x<1\), direct integration gives
\[
 0\le -\log(1-x)-x
 =\int_0^x\frac{s}{1-s}\,ds
 \le \frac{x^2}{2(1-x)}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(m_n\ge1\), and application with \(x=c/t\) gives
\[
 \left|\log\eta_n+c\sum_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\frac1t\right|
 \le \frac{c^2}{2(1-c/(m_n+1))}
      \sum_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\frac1{t^2}.
\]
Since \(m_n/n\to a_\star>0\), the right-hand side is \(O(n^{-1})\). Monotonicity of \(x\mapsto x^{-1}\) yields
\[
 \log\!\left(\frac{n+1}{m_n+1}\right)
 \le \sum_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\frac1t
 \le \log\!\left(\frac n{m_n}\right),
\]
and both outer terms converge to \(\log(1/a_\star)\). Consequently,
\[
 \log\eta_n\longrightarrow-c\log(1/a_\star)=c\log a_\star,
 \qquad
 \eta_n\longrightarrow a_\star^c.
\]

We now show that restriction to \(V_n\) gives a common subprobability component of the two complete experiments. The deterministic conditional assignment probabilities imply, by the same conditioning induction, that the assignment vector has the same law under both signs. If \(t\le m_n\), then \(t/n\le a_\star\), and hence \(Y_{nt}^+(1)=Y_{nt}^-(1)=0\). If \(t>m_n\), the event \(V_n\) forces \(A_{nt}=0\), so the observed outcome is \(Y_{nt}^\sigma(0)=0\) under either sign. The propensity and regression logs are the same deterministic arrays under both signs. Thus, for every measurable set \(H\),
\[
 \Pr_+\{(O_n,U)\in H,\,V_n\}
 =\Pr_-\{(O_n,U)\in H,\,V_n\}
 =:\nu_n(H).
\]
Independence and the common law of \(U\) preserve this equality when the confidence set is randomized. The common subprobability measure has mass \(\nu_n(\Omega)=\eta_n\) and is dominated by each sign-specific law.

Define
\[
 E_{\sigma,n}=\{\tau_n^\sigma\in D_n(O_n,U)\},
 \qquad
 \gamma_n=\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
             \Pr_\sigma(E_{\sigma,n}^{c}).
\]
The honesty premise implies \(\limsup_n\gamma_n\le\alpha\). Since \(\nu_n\) is the restriction of either sign-specific law to \(V_n\),
\[
 \nu_n(E_{\sigma,n}^{c})
 \le \Pr_\sigma(E_{\sigma,n}^{c})
 \le\gamma_n.
\]
The union bound under \(\nu_n\) gives
\[
 \nu_n(E_{+,n}\cap E_{-,n})
 \ge\eta_n-2\gamma_n.
\]
On this intersection the same set \(D_n(O_n,U)\) contains both causal estimands. Proposition \texttt{prop:parameterized-late-ramp-membership} gives their finite-sample separation, so
\[
 \operatorname{diam}(D_n)
 \ge|\tau_n^+-\tau_n^-|
 \ge\delta(1-a_\star).
\]
Dominance of \(\nu_n\) by either experimental law therefore implies, for each sign,
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\!\left\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)
       \ge\delta(1-a_\star)\right\}
 \ge\eta_n-2\gamma_n.
\]
Taking lower limits, using \(\eta_n\to a_\star^c\), and using \(\limsup_n\gamma_n\le\alpha\), we obtain
\[
 \liminf_n\Pr_\sigma\!\left\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)
       \ge\delta(1-a_\star)\right\}
 \ge a_\star^c-2\alpha.
\]
The right side is positive exactly in the asserted nontrivial regime. Every step used only the two fixed potential-outcome experiments, their randomization laws, and complete-log measurability; no estimator limit law entered.
body.justification: The theorem gives the requested bounded-hazard probability--diameter tradeoff for every randomized confidence set measurable from the complete log.
body.gap: Gaussian adaptive-inference theory excludes these nonnegligible increments, while existing width bounds do not exploit the common sequential subprobability component of mass \(a_\star^c\) supported on the void event.
body.consumer: Designers can read off when a target diameter is impossible from the allocation intensity \(c\), ramp start \(a_\star\), outcome scale \(\delta\), and desired miscoverage \(\alpha\).
